The Idea

It doesn't defend. It conducts.

Peace with teeth is the calm with the bite.

Peace is what you want — never the fight. You keep the strength to stand if you have to, so you're free to choose peace. The teeth aren't for using. They're for being real.

You don't react; you conduct. You're in the center, and things move around you — not the other way around. And if you're aware, ahead of it, you never end up in the fight at all. That's the whole point.

The Training

It's a fight to find the peace.

Forty years in, this is what I train for. Two fights, run together — the outer and the inner. The strength doesn't need to be used. It needs to be real.

01

The outer fight

The body and the skill, kept genuine. Train daily. Keep the water boiling. The years compound — that's the whole secret, and there's no shortcut around it.

02

The inner fight

The harder one. Warfare against the self — the ego, the fear, the reflex to react. It never really ends, and it's what sharpens you.

03

The peace

Further down the road you avoid the fight before it starts. People sense the strength and step back. That's the peace the teeth are for.

Warfare against the self is enlightenment.

"Though one may conquer a thousand times a thousand men in battle, he who conquers himself is the greatest victor." — The Dhammapada

The Founder

Michael Weiner. 62. 40 years.

Forty years leaves you more than technique — a way to live, and that's different than most.

Karate, yoga, jiu-jitsu, Muay Thai, MMA. You learn to read a room in an instant. Read a person — their whole life running backward and forward, their movements before they move.

Enfighten is the path I've been on for many a decade — put into a mark, into gear, into the world. Into existence.

Train daily. Keep the water boiling. Think on the questions. Life will unfold — and you're in the perfect place you need to be.
